meta.note: DOIs resolved on Crossref; numbers from OpenAlex abstracts. Tag 'sci' = rule direction matches a real phenomenon; all coefficients remain game.
off_limits: white iron-free scaly-foot population (unverified; candidate nakamura2012)

rules.f_rule: Adult scale x TSR(heat): cold newborns bigger (plastic)
rules.phenomenon: Temperature-size rule: ectotherms reared colder mature larger; -5.0%/degC mass aquatic vs -0.5%/degC terrestrial (~100 mg dry mass)
rules.slide_line: Raise most cold-blooded animals in the cold and they grow up bigger. Ours do too.

rules.f_rule: R6 explanation: cold slows reactions -> giant
rules.phenomenon: Oxygen supply vs demand is the leading explanation of TSR and polar gigantism; contested
rules.slide_line: Polar seas grow giants. Why is still argued.

rules.f_rule: Cold -> giant (endotherm analogy)
rules.phenomenon: Bergmann's rule: 78/110 mammal species larger at higher latitude; heat-conservation mechanism, different from TSR

rules.f_rule: Size boost from buoyancy (1+0.6*rho_air*buoy)
rules.phenomenon: Buoyant support relaxes skeletal size limits [INFERRED]; island rule is food/predator driven and not modelled

rules.f_rule: (missing) oxygen -> size
rules.phenomenon: Palaeozoic giant insects under hyperoxia; some insects develop/evolve larger in hyperoxia
rules.slide_line: Giant insects lived when the air was oxygen-rich.

rules.f_rule: Si+O plates cheap, C plates expensive: cost ~ 1/(0.2+si)
rules.phenomenon: Biomineral is cheap: diatom silicification ~2% of energy budget; shell cost lies in organic matrix
rules.slide_line: Building a glass shell costs a diatom about 2% of its energy.

rules.f_rule: Recipe -> plate composition (armour from available minerals)
rules.phenomenon: Scaly-foot snail iron sulfide (pyrite+greigite) sclerites; goethite limpet teeth; silica sponges/diatoms/grasses
rules.slide_line: At a deep-sea vent, a snail builds its armour out of iron.

rules.f_rule: Hunger -> plates via selection (R10)
rules.phenomenon: Escalation / Mesozoic marine revolution: armour and predators ratchet together
rules.slide_line: When shell-crushers evolved, snails got thicker shells.

rules.f_rule: Hunger x Development cell is empty (section 7 matrix)
rules.phenomenon: Inducible defences: Daphnia helmets/neckteeth on predator cues, transgenerational; grass silica induced by grazing
rules.slide_line: Water fleas that smell a predator grow a helmet, and so do their babies.

rules.f_rule: Gape limit (S > gape*0.8 uneatable); rods/spikes defence
rules.phenomenon: Gape-limited predation; stickleback spines vs perch/pike
rules.slide_line: A stickleback's spines make it too big to swallow.

rules.f_rule: Horns pay as attack under Hunger (R10)
rules.phenomenon: Horns/antlers are mostly sexually selected weapons, not predation tools

rules.f_rule: Si plates block water dissolution of Si tissue (R5)
rules.phenomenon: Ocean dissolves biogenic silica: ~3% preserved; organic coat protects diatom glass (reverse of F)
rules.slide_line: Only about 3% of the glass ocean life makes reaches the seafloor.

rules.f_rule: Si+O builders -> spires/reefs (R12)
rules.phenomenon: Modern hexactinellid glass sponge reefs off British Columbia; diatom ooze
rules.slide_line: Glass sponges still build reefs off Canada.

rules.f_rule: Si -> hexagonal facets, stepped profile, 15-degree joints (R1 at body scale)
rules.phenomenon: Biosilica is amorphous; silica builders make lattices (Euplectella cage) but not crystal facets; fibres flex via organics
rules.slide_line: Venus's flower basket builds a glass lattice tower.

rules.f_rule: Si biases radial symmetry order 3/6
rules.phenomenon: Radial silica protists exist, but radial symmetry is common in carbon life too; no causal link

rules.f_rule: Eye area A = g19*(1.5 - light): darker -> bigger eyes
rules.phenomenon: Dim light -> bigger eyes (deep sea), but total darkness -> eye loss (cavefish; vision 15% of resting metabolism at 1 g)
rules.slide_line: In a cave, eyes cost a young fish 15% of its energy, so evolution switched them off.

rules.f_rule: Eye cost 0.2*A^2
rules.phenomenon: Sensory/neural tissue is energetically expensive

rules.f_rule: Glow needs O (glow eyes o>0.3; patches ~ o)
rules.phenomenon: Bioluminescence is luciferin oxidation; coelenterazine possibly began as antioxidant
rules.slide_line: Living light burns oxygen.

rules.f_rule: Dark -> glow wins (R8)
rules.phenomenon: 76% of observed water-column individuals 0-3900 m off California are bioluminescent
rules.slide_line: Three in four animals in the deep sea make their own light.

rules.f_rule: Glowing flora -> grazers carry spores
rules.phenomenon: Glowing fungi attract insects; glow under circadian control

rules.f_rule: Thick air -> float mode, hover cost ~ max(0, rho_body - rho_air) (R11)
rules.phenomenon: Titan 1467 hPa / 93.7 K -> ~5.3 kg/m3 [INFERRED], ~4x Earth but ~200x thinner than flesh; floating needs gas bags (siphonophores, Sagan-Salpeter floaters)
rules.slide_line: On Titan the air is four times thicker and gravity a seventh of ours.

rules.f_rule: Walk cost per metre ~ M/(sqrt(nLimbs)*len)
rules.phenomenon: Cost of transport inversely proportional to effective limb length (98% of variance, no independent mass effect)
rules.slide_line: Long legs make walking cheap.

rules.f_rule: segN gene + segment duplication mutation -> serpents
rules.phenomenon: Segmentation clock sets segment number; fast clock gives snakes hundreds of vertebrae
rules.slide_line: A snake's segment clock just ticks faster.

rules.f_rule: Hox-like domains; limbStart/limbEnd open/close legs
rules.phenomenon: Hox genes set segment identity; Ubx change suppresses abdominal legs in insects
rules.slide_line: Insects have six legs because one gene says no legs on the abdomen.

rules.f_rule: Worm founders -> complexity fast
rules.phenomenon: Cambrian appearance of body plans; earlier divergence, later ecological success
rules.slide_line: Most animal body plans appear within a geological blink.

rules.f_rule: Basal cost b0*M^0.75*rate(heat)
rules.phenomenon: Kleiber scaling + Boltzmann temperature term (MTE); exponent varies 2/3-1
rules.slide_line: Bigger animals burn less energy per gram.

rules.f_rule: Lifespan ~ S^0.25/rate(heat)
rules.phenomenon: Ectotherms live longer in colder places within species, as MTE predicts
rules.slide_line: Cold-water animals of the same species live longer.

rules.f_rule: Sociality dilution /(1+0.15n)
rules.phenomenon: Selfish herd

rules.f_rule: Colour = composition (R9, skin hash)
rules.phenomenon: Diet/mineral pigments (carotenoids, iron sulfide), structural colour; element->hue palette invented
rules.slide_line: Flamingos are pink because of what they eat.

rules.f_rule: Plates stain with age towards sea colour (R3)
rules.phenomenon: No source for a per-sea palette

rules.f_rule: Si flora spineRods cut grazing 60%
rules.phenomenon: Silica phytoliths wear herbivore mandibles; grazing induces silica
rules.slide_line: Grass fights back with glass.

rules.f_rule: Dim -> flora reach tall, no caps (R7)
rules.phenomenon: Shade avoidance: stems elongate in shade

rules.f_rule: Stress mutagenesis x2.5 after dial moves
rules.phenomenon: Shown in bacteria (Galhardo et al. 2007); not established in animals

rules.f_rule: C flexible vs Si rigid at organism scale (R1 -> bodies)
rules.phenomenon: Rigidity from mineralised composites, flexibility from organic polymers; Euplectella laminated glass overcomes brittleness
rules.slide_line: Every silicon body on Earth is glass, and glass doesn't bend.

change_suggestions.change: Make eye size hump-shaped: plastic growth with dimness only above light~0.15; below, let eye cost select eyes away unless local glow is common
change_suggestions.why: Cavefish lose eyes in total dark; deep-sea eyes persist because of bioluminescence

change_suggestions.change: Add inducible armour: newborn plateCover += k*Hunger*threat; Si flora spineRods up under grazing
change_suggestions.why: Daphnia helmets (transgenerational), grass silica induction; fills the empty Hunger x Development cell

change_suggestions.change: Retire 'Hunger makes horns' as science: hunter weapon = claws/gape; horns/spines = prey defence via gape limitation; otherwise tag horns [game]
change_suggestions.why: Horns are mostly sexually selected weapons

change_suggestions.change: Couple size cap to oxygen (S_max x (1+k*o)) and scale TSR amplitude by medium (swimmers full, walkers ~1/10)
change_suggestions.why: Hyperoxia giants; aquatic TSR ~10x terrestrial. F's 15x mass span is plausible only for aquatic

change_suggestions.change: Rewrite R6's explanation: oxygen supply vs demand (debated), not 'reactions slow'
change_suggestions.why: Direction is right, mechanism claim is not the accepted one

change_suggestions.change: Make flora glow scale with o too
change_suggestions.why: Keeps 'living light burns oxygen' true sim-wide

change_suggestions.change: Gate float mode on high buoy (gas-bag volume); don't claim dense air alone floats animals
change_suggestions.why: Titan air ~5 kg/m3 is ~200x thinner than flesh

change_suggestions.change: Templates by niche; chemistry sets style (facets, colour)
Allow template loss (decarcinisation) when niche disappears
Morph template parts allometrically: part = a*S^b
change_suggestions.why: Huxley allometry; capsule newborns, template adults

change_suggestions.change: Expose canalization strength as a declared knob; individual moulds by ontogeny, lineage template by selection

slide_facts.fact: At deep-sea vents in the Indian Ocean, a snail armours its foot with iron sulfide scales, the only living animal known to put iron sulfide in its skeleton.
Building a glass shell costs a diatom only about 2% of its energy budget.
Serengeti grasses that are grazed hard grow more glass in their leaves, and clipping them in the lab triggers it.
For a young Mexican cavefish, eyes and the visual brain cost 15% of resting energy, and the cave form lost them.
Three in four animals seen in the deep water off California can make their own light (76%, 0-3,900 m).
Warmth shrinks water animals about 5% in mass per degree, ten times more than land animals (~100 mg dry mass).
Evolution has turned crustaceans into crabs at least five separate times.
Only about 3% of the glass that ocean life makes survives into the seafloor; the sea dissolves the rest.

template_principles.phenomenon: Same functional problem -> same body; limited morphospace
template_principles.licenses: A short template list; different chemistries reaching the same template = convergence beat

template_principles.phenomenon: >=5 independent origins of crab-like form in decapods; repeated losses (decarcinization)
template_principles.licenses: Templates can be gained and lost

template_principles.phenomenon: Lamnid sharks and tunas converge mechanically; marine tetrapods converge in many innovations
Development buffers variation into a few stable outcomes (epigenetic landscape)
template_principles.licenses: Templates as attractors; pull strength is a game coefficient

template_principles.phenomenon: Shared trochophore larva in annelids and molluscs, very different adults; widespread metamorphosis
template_principles.licenses: Every creature starts as the same tiny capsule

template_principles.phenomenon: Parts grow as y = a*x^b; shape changes with size
template_principles.licenses: Morph template parts as power laws of body size (b>1 for horns/legs/frills)

templates.analogue: Gelatinous drifters convergent in medusae, ctenophores, salps (chordates); siphonophore gas floats
templates.slide_line: Jellyfish, comb jellies and salps look alike but aren't related. Salps are closer kin to you.

templates.analogue: Snakelike limb-reduced form evolved ~25 times in squamates; eels, caecilians
templates.slide_line: Lizards have turned snake-shaped about 25 separate times.

templates.analogue: Rotation rare in nature; useful only on flat open ground or low Reynolds number (dung beetles, tumbleweeds, flagella; rolling stomatopod); spirals = shell coiling
templates.slide_line: Nature almost never invents the wheel. Dung beetles and tumbleweeds are the exceptions.

templates.analogue: Carcinisation >=5 times; armoured grazers recur; bipedal hopping convergent in desert rodents (unpredictable escape)
templates.slide_line: Evolution has turned crustaceans into crabs at least five separate times.

templates.analogue: Fast hunters converge (lamnids/tunas; ichthyosaurs/dolphins/sharks); elongate ambush hunters (morays); frills->turn rate invented
templates.slide_line: Sharks, ichthyosaurs and dolphins: three hunters, one shape.

templates.analogue: Reef building in corals, sponges, oysters, tube worms, bryozoans; ecosystem engineers
templates.slide_line: Sponges, corals, oysters and worms each learned to build reefs on their own.

templates.analogue: Long-legged stilt walkers recur; limb length explains 98% of walking cost variance
templates.slide_line: Long legs are the cheapest way to walk.

templates.analogue: Head horns evolved repeatedly (rhinos, ceratopsians, horned lizards, chameleons), mainly sexually selected
templates.slide_line: Horns evolved again and again, mostly to win mates.

templates.analogue: Giant planktivores recur: baleen whales, whale/basking sharks, mantas, 100-Myr pachycormid dynasty; aerial floaters hypothetical
templates.slide_line: Giant plankton-eaters keep evolving, including a giant-fish dynasty that lasted 100 million years.
